b1-review-1.R1.1 Gap Year Diaries: a special episode:
Danny: Welcome to a special episode of Gap Year Diaries! I'm recording in the café where I met Ana on my first week in São Paulo. And today I have two guests: Ana and my roommate, Bruno.
Ana: Hi everyone! I remember that day. Danny asked me for directions, and then we discovered that we both know Tom.
Danny: A mutual friend! So, Bruno, how would you describe me when I first arrived?
Bruno: Honestly? You were a bit shy, and you tended to stay in the room playing video games. You've changed a lot.
Danny: I used to play for hours every day. Now I hardly ever play. And you can be quite messy, Bruno!
Bruno: That's true. Deep down, I'm a very organized person. My clothes just don't know it.
Ana: And Danny looks different, too. He's been growing a beard for two months.
Bruno: He looks like a pirate.
Danny: Thanks, guys. So, what's new in your lives? Ana, you work in an emergency department. How's work?
Ana: Hectic, as usual. I've been working twelve-hour shifts all month, so I'm exhausted. But last week my cousin Carol visited, and Danny picked her up at the airport.
Danny: The woman with red curly hair and big round glasses. I found her in two minutes!
Bruno: And Danny persuaded me to keep running with our group. We've been training for the ten-K race in December.
Danny: I've stopped eating junk food, and I hope to finish in less than an hour.
Ana: And how's the new job?
Danny: Great! I've been working as a guide for three weeks now. I'm a freelancer, so I don't have to work every day, but I have to know a lot of history. Last Sunday, another guide was sick, so I filled in for him. And a hotel offered me a full-time job, but I turned it down.
Bruno: Smart. You don't want to spend your gap year at a reception desk.
Danny: Last question. Bruno, your parents met in a hospital. How are people meeting now?
Bruno: Online, of course. More and more people are using apps. My friends have all met their partners on their phones.
Ana: Things have changed so much. My grandparents met at a church party!
Danny: Well, that's all for today. Thanks for listening!

b1-review-1.R1.3 Dialogues:
Narrator: Dialogue one.
Carol: Hi! You must be Danny. Ana told me what you look like.
Danny: Hi Carol! Welcome to Brazil. How was your flight?
Carol: Long! I never sleep on planes. Have you been living here for long?
Danny: For about three months. I've been working as a tour guide.
Carol: Really? I'd love to do a tour.
Danny: Would you? I'll take you on Saturday!
Narrator: Dialogue two.
Bruno: You look tired. What have you been doing?
Danny: I've been studying the history of the city all morning. I have to give a tour tomorrow.
Bruno: Do you have to wear a uniform?
Danny: No, I don't have to. But I mustn't be late. Tourists hate waiting.
Bruno: And the hotel job? Did you take it?
Danny: No, I turned it down. I want to keep traveling.
